environment: Node VM running actual nitnem/reader.js and actual local-learning.js; synthetic DOM, records, and controlled write/editor locks
scope: Async dialog lifetimes, captured-bani persistence, draft preservation, editor leases, import/export/update, and real-versus-programmatic scroll intent
dataPolicy: Only invented SYNTHETIC learning data; no user browser or saved learning accessed

checks.name: A delayed file read from a closed dialog cannot import or change another bani editor
An import already waiting for its write lock stays bound to the old bani and preserves its lease until completion
Close freezes editing while saving and preserves a newer programmatic draft instead of closing it
Explicit Save permits continued typing, keeps the later draft and marks it unsaved
A late export after a switch creates no download and cannot alter the new editor
An ordinary export uses the captured bani and contains the saved reflection
A late bookmark completes only in the original record and leaves a new dialog unchanged
A saved-line navigation waiting on an old note cannot close or move the new bani
A current saved-line navigation saves its reflection and then moves to the selected line
An obsolete lease result never replaces the lease of a newly opened dialog
A queued close event from the previous dialog does not retire a newly opened session
A stale close completion cannot close a newly opened dialog for the same bani
Before-update freezes a pending reflection, rejects a stale session and preserves the new editor
An active import blocks overlapping close and update until it completes
Save failures keep the draft visible and selectable, block close and update, and preserve stored bytes
A failed import restores its controls and leaves the existing note unchanged
Programmatic scrolling alone remains suppressed and does not overwrite the selected reading place
A real wheel intent ends suppression and persists the visible reading line
A real touchmove intent ends suppression and persists the visible reading line
A real keydown intent ends suppression and persists the visible reading line
Synthetic events, text-field arrows and unrelated keys do not cancel programmatic-scroll suppression
